about: LUKE is the Washington label of Thomas and Kristin Vogele, who started it with the 2012 vintage to put a spotlight on the Wahluke Slope, one of the state’s warmest and driest corners. The wines have always been made at the Mattawa winery of the Milbrandt family’s Evergreen Family Wines, and in late 2025 Evergreen took LUKE into its portfolio, with the Vogeles staying on to guide it. At around $25 a bottle, the reds have built a reputation as some of Washington’s best values; the 2019 Merlot made Wine Spectator’s Top 100.

The Wahluke Slope is a broad, south-facing alluvial fan above the Columbia River. Long sunny days ripen the fruit fully, while cooler nights off the river help hold acidity, a balance consulting winemaker Peter Devison has pointed to as the heart of the style. New oak is used with restraint so the fruit stays in focus. The 2022 is 91% Merlot with 9% Cabernet Franc, which adds lift and a savory edge.

The winery describes dark red fruit, rounded tannins and a smooth finish, with plum, cherry and blackberry on the palate and notes of tobacco, cedar and clove. Wine Enthusiast found it fresh and lively, with tart raspberry, sandalwood and dried rose petal over silky tannins, while James Suckling noted an earthy, gravelly nose and black cherry and spice on a medium-bodied palate.
